title: The Door to the Pass
hook: Hold eastbound. A walker is already in the paint.
scene: Overcast midday daylight on a two-lane downtown street heading east, wet asphalt edge to edge. The Menace is STOPPED at the stop line, nose at the marked-crosswalk edge — not rolling, no tire spray, not parked in the junction. The full-width nose plow on the front bull bar points east at a person in a dark coat already on the white bars. That walker is the hold reason. Brick downtown blocks occupy the left third of the frame, their sidewalks meeting this same roadway. She is not cleared for the pass. Both cats are a sound in the closed carrier on the floor.
debrief: The Beetle is stopped at the stop line. A person is already in the crosswalk. Brick downtown shares that wet street on the left. She is not cleared for the pass.

source.teaching_target: Hold at the stop line for a person already in the marked crosswalk; not in-lane motion.

image_brief.camera_pose: Shallower high-oblique — not map-flat straight-down, not a steep three-quarter. Photoreal daylight aerial with readable depth. Overcast midday, pale gray-white sky. The faded pink Beetle is STOPPED at the stop line / marked-crosswalk edge, heading left-to-right. Full-width nose plow on the front bull bar points right at the hold reason: a person already in the paint (or cross traffic / a signal — a visible reason she is not cleared). NOT in-lane motion: no tire spray, no rolling. Continuous wet asphalt left edge to right edge. Brick downtown occupies the left third and shares this same street.
